To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
maize‐based snack with soy and tignut flour is a good source of protein, carbohydrate, and minerals.

the optimal blend of toasted maize flour, soy flour, and tigernuts flour for the production of maize-based snack is 75/100 g, 20/10 g, and 5 g, respectively, and that it is a good source of protein and minerals.
the addition of soybean and tigernuts flour in maize flour can be used to improve the nutritional quality of maize‐base snack.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of maize‐based cookie with soybean and tigernuts flours.
the optimization of the production of maize‐based snacks supplemented with soy and tiger nut flour.

the optimization of the production and quality evaluation (functional properties, pasting property, antioxidant, antiputrefactive, and amino acid composition) of maize‐based cookies supplemented with soy and tiger‐nut flour.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the production and quality of the maize‐based snack fortified with soy and tignernut flour were optimized and evaluated.
the three blends were good sources of protein and essential minerals.

the three blends of the composite flour had the best proximate and mineral composition, good functional, pasting, antioxidant, antitnutritional, and amino acids profiles, and the best sensory acceptability for production of maize‐based snacks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the production of maize-based cookies supplemented with soy flour and tiger-nut flour was optimized and the cookies produced from this combination were found to have high protein, carbohydrate, and mineral contents, which were acceptable by sensory evaluation.
the addition of soy and tigermut flour to maize flour in a 3:2:1 proportion is a good option in terms of nutritional value and sensory acceptability for a maize‐based snack.
the addition of soy and tigernet flour into the maize flour would be beneficial in the production of a healthy snack with high protein and micronutrients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the snack produced from the composite flour blend of toasted maize flour, soy flour, and tigernuts flour is a good source of nutrients, and it can be used as a healthy snack.

the production of a healthy maize‐based snack can be optimized using the response surface methodology and the proximate, mineral, amino acid, and sensory evaluation of the snack can be used as a tool to evaluate the quality of the snack.
the snack produced from the optimized composite flour is a good source of nutrients and can be used to meet the daily nutrient requirement of the consumers.
